top5.title: Trump administration reportedly authorized shipment of 900,000 AI chips to China
top5.description: The Trump administration approved the shipment of 900,000 artificial-intelligence chips to China.
top5.why: The reported approval of 900,000 AI-chip shipments to China could materially reshape US export controls, Nvidia’s market access and the broader US-China technology rivalry.

top5.title: Anthropic Makes Record Debut on Nasdaq
top5.description: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq on November 19 under the ticker ANT, after pricing its IPO at 83 dollars per share. The company sold 980 million shares for about 81.3 billion dollars and must now answer to both its shareholders and its users.
top5.why: Anthropic’s reported $81.3 billion Nasdaq debut marks a major test of investor appetite and public-market valuations for frontier AI companies.

top5.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon at a lower price than Carbon
top5.description: Google announced Gemini 4 Neon, a model positioned between Carbon and Hydrogen. It costs 3 dollars per million input tokens and 15 dollars per million output tokens, and Google says it is about 32% cheaper per task than Carbon in its default configuration.
top5.why: Google’s lower-priced Gemini 4 Neon intensifies the AI model price war and could pressure competitors’ margins and enterprise adoption strategies.

top5.title: The UK can no longer conceal its Apple data request
top5.description: The UK was forced to make public its requests for a backdoor into iCloud encryption. The relevant court sided with Apple on holding the case in public.
top5.why: The UK’s forced disclosure of its iCloud backdoor request creates a significant precedent for government access to encrypted services and Apple’s privacy policy.

top5.title: Intuit sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for 3.68 billion dollars
top5.description: Intuit has agreed to sell Mailchimp to Italian holding company Bending Spoons for about 3.68 billion dollars, less than one-third of the price paid in 2021. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approval.
top5.why: Intuit’s sale of Mailchimp for $3.68 billion—less than a third of its 2021 purchase price—highlights the sharp repricing of SaaS assets and the pressure on software portfolios.
